$comment: Pinned OpenRouter model and request shape for tools/autoresearch.py. Do not guess these values: `reasoning_effort` is a top-level parameter, NOT `reasoning.effort`, and OpenRouter rejects an effort it does not recognise with a 400 that enumerates the values it will take. `tools/autoresearch.py` reads this file, and fails loudly on a 400 that names reasoning_effort, printing the set the API just reported.
verification: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models -> this id is listed, name 'Space Bunny Alpha', context_length 1000000, supported_parameters includes reasoning_effort. A 1-token POST to the chat endpoint with reasoning_effort='max' returned 200; the same request with an unrecognised value returned HTTP 400 'expected one of "max"|"xhigh"|"high"|"medium"|"low"|"minimal"|"none"'. The reasoning object form {effort: ...} also works but cannot be combined with reasoning.max_tokens, so the top-level parameter is the one to use.
title: learn-micro-gpt autoresearch
pricing_note: prompt and completion are both priced at 0 on this model as of the verification date, so a session costs tokens rather than money. The harness still reports total token usage per experiment in the run record, because a free model today is not a promise about tomorrow.
